issues.legal_issue: A land transfer made after the statutory cutoff by a predecessor-in-interest must be disregarded when determining a successor’s ceiling area if the successor inherited the land before the assessment date and the transfer is not within an applicable exception.
material_facts: The landowner executed a gift of land after the statutory cutoff, and the land would have been surplus absent the gift.
The donor died before the assessment date, and the successor inherited the land before that date.
The transfer did not fall within either applicable exception.
issues.conclusion: The gift had to be ignored in determining the successor’s ceiling area. The gifted land was treated as remaining with the donor until death, then inherited by the successor, and counted in the successor’s holding on the assessment date.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 5(6) of the U.P. Imposition of Ceiling on Land Holdings Act, 1960, a transfer made after January 24, 1971, of land that would otherwise have been declared surplus is ignored, subject to the proviso’s exceptions. The provision applies to any transfer, not only one made by the tenure-holder whose ceiling area is being determined; it also reaches a transfer by that holder’s predecessor-in-interest where the holder inherited the land before June 8, 1973. This interpretation advances the provision’s purpose of preventing evasion of ceiling limits. Arjan Singh v. State of Punjab was distinguishable because it turned on the construction of a different statutory provision and did not govern this issue.

rule.if: ceiling_determination_proceeding and post_cutoff_transfer and would_be_surplus_without_transfer and predecessor_made_transfer and successor_inherited_before_assessment and transfer_within_no_exception

predicates.ceiling_determination_proceeding: The matter concerns determining a landholder’s ceiling area and surplus land.
predicates.post_cutoff_transfer: The land was transferred after the applicable statutory cutoff.
predicates.would_be_surplus_without_transfer: The land would have been declared surplus if the transfer had not occurred.
predicates.predecessor_made_transfer: The transfer was made by a predecessor-in-interest of the person whose ceiling area is being determined.
predicates.successor_inherited_before_assessment: The person whose ceiling area is being determined inherited the land before the assessment date.
predicates.transfer_within_no_exception: The transfer falls within neither an excluded category of transfer nor the qualifying good-faith transfer exception.
predicates.transferred_land_counted_in_successor_ho: The transferred land is counted as part of the successor’s holding for ceiling determination.

issues.definition: When a ceiling determination involves surplus land transferred after the cutoff by a predecessor and inherited by the successor before assessment, and no exception applies, the land is counted in the successor’s holding.
